title: Sir Henry Percy to Cecil, Norham 23 July 1559 (BL Add MS 4136 f.172, DECODE R9256)

documents.shelfmark: BL Add MS 4136 f.172 (Forbes Papers tracing); original TNA SP 52/1 (Bain, CSP Scotland I no. 501)

plaintext.source: Cecil's decipherment is on the original (Bain no. 501: 'A few words in cipher, deciphered by Cecill'); not online. The calendars print only the letter in summary.

transcription.source: DECODE image IMG_R9256_I43281_P.jpg (an 18th-century tracing of the cipher passages only)
transcription.notes: Four passages, 13 words; underline and dot marks read at high zoom; a tracing, so copying errors are possible.

system.summary: Pigpen-like box script with underline/dot modifiers and a few extra signs; not established whether letter substitution, name code or both.
system.notes: CSP Foreign no. 1045 says Percy wrote 'Knox' as a cipher sign on 22 July. Sibling key records R9257, R9260-R9262 are other systems.

prior_solution.where: Cecil's contemporary decipherment on the original at TNA SP 52/1 (not online); calendars (CSP Foreign I 1051, CSP Scotland I 501) give the letter's content in summary without saying which words were in cipher

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie to the model, set up Claude Code, and posed the problem with /goal. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Downloaded the single DECODE image; found it is a Forbes tracing of four cipher passages plus an unrelated 1562 Sturmius key.
Transcribed 63 signs in 13 words as shape+mark tokens.
CSP Foreign I 1045/1051 and Bain CSP Scotland I 498/501: letter calendared, 'a few words in cipher, deciphered by Cecill'; cipher words not identified.
Checked key records R9257, R9260-R9262 in the same volume for a box alphabet.
Rosicrucian pigpen (shape = cell of three letters, mark = position), all layouts.
Joint word-pattern constraint search under five mark policies, and trigram annealing.
Names from the calendar text (prior, knox, whytlaw, norham castle) placed on repeated words.

outcome.method_basis: The 63 signs of the Forbes tracing were attacked ciphertext-only (pattern search, pigpen layouts, constraint search, annealing, calendar-name cribs) without result; Cecil's decipherment exists on the TNA SP 52/1 original, which is not online.
outcome.notes: Too short to break without the key; Cecil's interlined decipherment on TNA SP 52/1 would settle it.
